evidence.label: Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless primitive inside AWS Lambda that gives each session its own isolated, stateful virtual machine.
Each session is its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated kernel, memory, disk, and network — up to 32 GB of RAM and 16 vCPUs, with full root inside.
At build time, Lambda starts your app and snapshots the running process; every launch resumes from that snapshot instead of cold-booting, so your server is already running when the MicroVM comes up.
Idle MicroVMs suspend and resume with full state intact.
Memory, disk, and processes persist across the session. You build from a standard Dockerfile, run up to eight hours, and there are no clusters, VPCs, or capacity planning to manage.
